note: Concept register only — nothing here edits canon; the implementation audit adjudicates. Beacon is the broad, airy directory take: seven large Home cards over the 12 inventory categories, summary-first provider manager, full-width copy flow.

home_card_mapping.note: The packet requires a complete documented mapping when Home shows fewer domains than the 12 inventory categories. This is that mapping; it is also rendered live on the Home cards (every category appears as a destination row with its count on exactly one card, and all 12 #/dest/<cat> routes stay first-class).

plan_owner_impacts.evidence: Beacon proves the spacious-directory composition: a bounded 1480px measure that stays composed at 2500px, seven icon/title/purpose cards with category sub-listings, a hero search over content, one scenario-gated critical banner, and a compact attention list. Motion is gentle scale/fade only (c08-enter, card lift); deep pages keep a sticky beacon bar (named Back, breadcrumb, persistent search, Close Settings).

All 828 rows render from PM2_INVENTORY via store.resolveRow/rowsFor; browsing reaches every row (subgroup sections + per-subgroup advanced disclosure). CONFLICT: the rev-2 canonical deep-link probe id system.health.diagnostics-verbosity is absent from this inventory; Beacon renders an honest 'not in this project's settings' surface for stale ids and lands system.health.platform-diagnostics exactly. The census discrepancy between probe registries and the inventory should be resolved before new ids are minted.

Summary-first provider pages answer the human questions as a status-card grid (connected, account in use, included, usage-end behavior, models, setup/repair) with the what-next ladder, before any tabbed detail. Explicit quick actions are honest: Set up appears only with a real setupOffer, Repair only when an installation truly offers repair, the local Ollama update stays refused with the manual-only reason, and the Cursor CLI setup tab renders official source + exact host/environment choice with sign-in as a separate step.

The copy transaction as a FULL-WIDTH page: steps across the top, selectable category tiles with counts, wide preview table (add/replace/unchanged/unavailable/conflict per row with current/incoming values and notes), credential-by-reference note, sticky confirm bar naming the restore point, staged atomic apply with verify, receipt with working rollback (walked end-to-end: 11 adds applied and restored exactly). One-time language throughout; no sync affordance exists.

Navigation is exclusively dest-object routing through PM2.route (cmd.settings.navigate family); search selection routes by rid only. The locate step resolves a focus rid back through PM2.search.resolveRid because the URL grammar carries manager/object/tab but not sectionId — a real contract detail the command family should record.

Permissions & FileSafe renders from the shared manager view model in Beacon's grammar (status cards + rows + advanced drawers); managed rows carry origin in Details. No new permission semantics are minted here.

Row states normal/managed/unavailable/restart-required/reconnect-required/changed-elsewhere/error all render with state notes and silhouette-differentiated chips; interactive controls suppress value-echo chips so the chip vocabulary carries only extra meaning (managed, unavailable, differs, recommended, not-set).

Keystone traces registered in candidate-wiring-delta.json, all flagged concept_local_state: value set with validation, search landing sequence, copy preview/apply/rollback, provider triggers, missing-setting fallback.

Token-only styling across all 8 themes (verified in glass-light and retro-dark); one backdrop-filter layer total (the shared titlebar); reduced-motion behavior relies on the three pm-shell kill switches and no JS transitionend dependency.

Explicit ui state machine (view/menu/search/copy/all facets), stable model ids everywhere, All Settings windowed at ~27 live rows against 2,828 records under stress, popup menus and drawers as data-driven state — no DOM-geometry-derived semantics.
